sources.title: Post Falls considers fundraising to preserve Spokane Street tower
sources.sourceType: local news report quoting city officials
sources.licenseNotes: Citation only; source material retains publisher terms.
notes: Quotes the Post Falls public works director identifying 1908 as the construction year and explaining that the tower has not functioned as a City water-division asset for years because its pressure does not meet modern standards.
Reports that the tower sits between First and Second avenues, the area became a mini park through downtown planning, and preservation work was under consideration.

sources.title: Post Falls Rotary launches campaign to preserve historic water tower
sources.sourceType: local news report and preservation announcement
sources.licenseNotes: Citation only; source material retains publisher terms.
notes: Reports that the tower no longer stores water, remained in service for more than 70 years, and is the subject of a Post Falls Rotary preservation campaign.
Reports that recent engineering review found the historic structure sound for its age and that the City Council allocated estimated demolition cost as seed funding for preservation.

sources.title: City of Post Falls Water System Master Plan
sources.licenseNotes: Public city planning document; cite rather than mirror until reuse terms are reviewed.
notes: Table 1-3 lists Ford Rock as a 0.26 MG welded-steel Main Zone tank constructed in 1979, with a 65-foot diameter, base elevation 2,275 feet, and overflow elevation 2,299 feet.
Pages 1-6, 3-7, 4-1, and 4-5 identify Ford Rock as inactive; page 4-5 states that the City had no plans to put it back into service.
Table 1-3 lists Reilly #1 and #2 as active 1.0 MG precast-concrete Main Zone tanks, with base elevation 2,332 feet, overflow elevation 2,356 feet, and 85-foot diameters.
Table 1-3 dates Reilly #1 to 1986 and Reilly #2 to 1994; page 4-5 instead dates Reilly #1 to 1983 while retaining 1994 for Reilly #2.
Page 3-7 identifies the Reilly Tanks as active storage serving the Main and Highlands zones.
